clue.text: Still wearing specs to take in constant opportunities for learning

parts.note: still, as in 'still more', means even
wearing a coat is being in it

indicators.note: to take in means the word for specs swallows the constant's letter

parts.note: specs is short for spectacles, glasses
C is the standard symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: Someone who is still in glasses squints to read about a mathematical constant.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening classes are adult education courses held after the working day, chances to learn something new.

clue.text: Voyager's requirement for space needs a selective copy fashioned

indicators.note: fashioned means made or shaped, so these letters are formed into something new

explanation.surface: A spacecraft seems to need a carefully chosen copy of something made for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Voyager probes had to reach the speed needed to break free of a body's gravity before heading into deep space.

clue.text: Obscure magazines imported by eastern European

indicators.note: imported by means the magazines are carried inside the two single-letter abbreviations

parts.note: clips are ammunition magazines that feed a gun

explanation.surface: Some hard-to-find periodicals are brought in by an Eastern European importer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magazines' suggests periodicals, but here it is the ammunition sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure something is to block it from view, as the moon does to the sun during a solar event.

clue.text: Once I'm up I set on American, having little or no money

indicators.note: set means arranged or put in order, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Once out of bed, someone bets on an American and ends up broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply joins the anagram to US.
explanation.definitionFit: Impecunious is a formal word for penniless or hard up.

clue.text: World travel, crossing line on Beagle, intermittently

indicators.note: crossing means the word for travel goes across, enclosing, the line's letter

parts.note: to go is to travel

indicators.note: intermittently means taking every other letter of the ship's name, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A round-the-world voyage on the Beagle, Darwin's ship, carried on in fits and starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just joins the pieces; HMS Beagle carried Charles Darwin around the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: World used as an adjective, as in a world war or world tour, means worldwide, covering the entire planet.

clue.text: Ineffective type made off, coming into fortune

indicators.note: coming into means the jumbled letters go inside the word for fortune

parts.note: fortune and luck are synonyms

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A useless character ran away just as he inherited a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made off' reads as running away, but 'off' is only the anagram signal for 'made'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lame duck is a weak, failing person or business, or an official serving out a term with no power left.

clue.text: Notice abandoning good for evil

indicators.note: abandoning means the letter for good is dropped from the word for notice

parts.note: a notice put up is a sign

explanation.surface: A notice tells people to forsake good and embrace wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sin and evil are both words for wrongdoing, with the noun sense of wickedness.

clue.text: High spirits of nephew, say, losing head

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the word for a nephew is taken off

parts.note: a nephew is an example of a relation

explanation.surface: A nephew's cheerful mood is lost when he loses his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the nephew as one example of a relation.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is a feeling of great happiness and exhilaration, the same as being in high spirits.

clue.text: Go if desperate — a spread such as this!

definitions.text: Go if desperate — a spread such as this!

indicators.note: spread means scattered about, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: An encouragement to try this rich spread when in need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' does double duty: the anagram signal, and in the whole clue the kind of food the answer is.
explanation.definitionFit: Foie gras paste is a luxury goose or duck liver spread, served on toast.

clue.text: Charlie plays around with love song

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: around means the letters of plays are moved about into a new order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Charlie fools around, playing a love song.
explanation.definitionFit: A calypso is a type of West Indian song, often witty and topical.

clue.text: Part of Vermont — an awful state

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone complains about part of Vermont being dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: Vermont is a red herring: it is itself a state, but the answer is another.
explanation.definitionFit: Montana is a large state in the north-western United States.

clue.text: Just beat seed

definitions.meaning: to ... a rival is to beat them by a tiny margin, as in pipped at the post
a small fruit seed, as in an apple or orange

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers a narrow win as a verb and a small fruit kernel as a noun.

clue.text: Almost doomed by family secret

parts.note: a clan is an extended family

indicators.note: Almost means the last letter of the word for doomed is dropped

parts.note: doomed and destined both mean fated

explanation.surface: A family's secret leaves it nearly doomed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets the family beside the shortened word.
explanation.definitionFit: Clandestine means kept secret or done covertly.

clue.text: Second right-wing counter of votes may be a liar

parts.note: a Tory is a member of Britain's right-of-centre Conservative Party
a teller counts the votes in an election or Parliamentary division

explanation.surface: A Conservative who counts votes for a second time could be dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: In Parliament, tellers count the members voting in each lobby.
explanation.definitionFit: A fibber is sometimes called a teller of stories; the answer can be a liar, though not every one is.

clue.text: Queen once rejected after struggle for city in Europe

indicators.note: after means the reversed name follows the word for struggle

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete

indicators.note: rejected means the queen's name is sent back, so read backwards

parts.note: Ann, the old spelling seen in Queen Ann's lace, was Queen of Great Britain from 1702 to 1714

explanation.surface: A former queen was turned away after a fight over a European city.
explanation.definitionFit: Vienna is the capital of Austria, a major city in central Europe.

clue.text: Cadge from miser, importing one in France for nothing

indicators.note: importing means the French word is brought into the miser's name
for means the French word takes the place of the zero

parts.note: Scrooge is the miser of Dickens's A Christmas Carol
nothing is zero, which looks like O
un is French for one

explanation.surface: Someone begs from a skinflint, bringing in a French coin for free.
explanation.definitionFit: To cadge and to scrounge both mean to get something by begging, without paying.

clue.text: Last on is hardly concealing shock

indicators.note: concealing means the words before it hide the answer across their spaces

explanation.surface: The last item on the bill is hardly a shock.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish someone is to surprise or amaze them, a verb sense of shock.

clue.text: Sort of clue needed in case of love game

indicators.note: needed in means the clue type goes inside the outer letters
case of means the outside letters of love, its shell

parts.note: a crossword clue is either an across or a down clue

explanation.surface: A crossword hint needed for a love story.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team game played with netted sticks.

clue.text: University officer taken in by remedy for society

indicators.note: taken in by means the first pieces go inside the word for remedy

parts.note: a cure is a remedy
Lt is the abbreviation for Lieutenant, an army officer

explanation.surface: A university officer is fooled by a social cure-all.
explanation.definitionFit: Culture can mean a particular society or civilisation, with its customs and way of life.

clue.text: Unusual Monday person full of energy

indicators.note: Unusual means out of the normal order, so the letters of the weekday are rearranged

explanation.surface: It is unusual to find someone energetic on a Monday.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a generator; figuratively, a tirelessly energetic and forceful person.

clue.text: Sale requiring caution to be exercised

indicators.note: exercised means worked or moved about, so the word's letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Buyers are warned to take care at a sale.
explanation.definitionFit: An auction is a public sale where goods go to the highest bidder.

clue.text: A benefit adopted by North America produces disgust

indicators.note: adopted by means the pieces are taken into the abbreviation

parts.note: use, as in 'what's the use?', means benefit

explanation.surface: A welfare payment adopted across the continent causes revulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea is sickness, and figuratively a feeling of revulsion or loathing.

clue.text: Church collecting ancient stone, gold and silver in abeyance

indicators.note: collecting means the church gathers the other pieces inside it

parts.note: CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England
ancient means old
st is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight
or is gold in heraldry
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A church gathers old stones, gold and silver, to be stored away.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan put into cold storage is shelved or set aside for later, the idiomatic sense of in abeyance.

clue.text: People in line for audience must be prompt

indicators.note: for audience means the word is as heard by listeners

parts.note: a queue is a line of people waiting their turn

explanation.surface: Theatregoers queueing need to be punctual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is a signal to an actor to speak or enter; as a verb, to prompt.

clue.text: High roller's note about star in the morning

indicators.note: about means the note goes around the other pieces

parts.note: ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
the Sun is a star
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: A big gambler's IOU about a celebrity, written in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High roller' suggests a big gambler; here it is a tall rolling wave.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge sea wave, humorously a high roller since waves roll in.

clue.text: Voice impression

explanation.definitionFit: One word means both to express publicly, as a verb, and a manner or appearance, as a noun.

clue.text: Military man disposed of one, very disheartened

parts.note: goods disposed of have been sold
one is I in Roman numerals

indicators.note: disheartened here means reduced to its heart, keeping only the middle letters of very

explanation.surface: A soldier got rid of one comrade and felt very low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' normally means losing the middle; here it is read as keeping only the core, ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier is a serviceman in an army.

clue.text: Officer's examination papers?

parts.note: not papers for a test an officer sits but the court documents a police officer needs before inspecting premises

explanation.definitionFit: A court order lets police enter and inspect a property, which is the examination meant here.
